name: Tarf
description: A star 93 parsecs away, 48 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 40526: radius 48.474 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 598.297 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.063) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 40526: effective temperature 4103 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.076)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 1.28 from 2024A&A...682A.145S; the 19 published values span log g 0.98 to 2.05, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.2% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 40526: distance 93.023 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.018), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 93 parsecs away, 48 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 598 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,103 K, so 48.474 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 40526: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Beta Cancri
quotes.card: Beta Cancri is the brightest star in the zodiacal constellation of Cancer.
quotes.introduction: It is visible to the naked eye with an apparent visual magnitude of +3.5, and has an absolute magnitude of −1.2.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 3098404220680931968 (quality A), from 2005A&A...430..165F; Gaia DR3 measures none
